issue.title: CI fails: CMake Error (non-target-directive) at src/secp256k1/cmake/TryAppendCFlags.cmake:22 (add_compile_options):   Use of non-target directives is not recommended.  Consider   target_compile_options instead.

events.body:
> Not sure why this wasn't caught by one of the nightly CIs

Somewhat related, but in future, it would be good to actually explain in these kinds of PRs, that they are fixing issues that will cause fairly imminent CI failures, and require backporting to all branches. 

#36889 didn't mention this at all, and #36890 was opened without the CMake fix, and doesn't mention it. I'd imagine most reviewers might not realise the underlying issues, and their effects, if they just read something like "fixes CMake warnings".

My understanding is that this doesn't need backport. It is just a harmless warning? However, it breaks the CI in the repo here.

Maybe we should re-visit this and exclude the errors there?

```diff
ci: Exclude cmake warnings-as-errors on "mutable" tasks

Those tasks may update cmake over night, so new warnings can lead to errors and ci failures.

It would be better to track those issues in a dedicated nightly CI.

diff --git a/.github/ci-windows.py b/.github/ci-windows.py
index ba48808..b12fa0f 100755
--- a/.github/ci-windows.py
+++ b/.github/ci-windows.py
@@ -31,3 +31,3 @@ GENERATE_OPTIONS = {
         "-DBUILD_UTIL_CHAINSTATE=ON",
-        "-DCMAKE_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR=ON",
+        "-DCMAKE_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR=OFF",
     ],
@@ -37,3 +37,3 @@ GENERATE_OPTIONS = {
         "-DBUILD_FOR_FUZZING=ON",
-        "-DCMAKE_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR=ON",
+        "-DCMAKE_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR=OFF",
     ],
diff --git a/ci/test/00_setup_env_mac_native.sh b/ci/test/00_setup_env_mac_native.sh
index d2e35b9..57971c4 100755
--- a/ci/test/00_setup_env_mac_native.sh
+++ b/ci/test/00_setup_env_mac_native.sh
@@ -17,2 +17,3 @@ printf -v BITCOIN_CONFIG "%q " \
   --preset=dev-mode \
+  -DCMAKE_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR=OFF \
   -DWITH_USDT=OFF \
diff --git a/ci/test/00_setup_env_mac_native_fuzz.sh b/ci/test/00_setup_env_mac_native_fuzz.sh
index b21edb4..789c448 100755
--- a/ci/test/00_setup_env_mac_native_fuzz.sh
+++ b/ci/test/00_setup_env_mac_native_fuzz.sh
@@ -11,2 +11,3 @@ printf -v BITCOIN_CONFIG "%q " \
  -DBUILD_FOR_FUZZING=ON \
+ -DCMAKE_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR=OFF \
  -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS="-Wl,-stack_size -Wl,0x80000" \

> However, it breaks the CI in the repo here.

Yea, that's why it needs backport (absent other changes), along with the other CMake change already put into the backport PRs. Devs have also already reported this breaking their local builds, so changing the CI in the release branches also isn't a complete fix (absent telling devs to change their workflows).

https://gnusha.org/bitcoin-core-dev/2026-11-17.log:
> 10:01 < achow101> Updated cmake and started getting these errors in my builds: Use of non-target directives is not recommended.  Consider target_compile_definitions instead.

Hmm, I guess there is no correct answer here, only tradeoffs :(

* `-DCMAKE_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR=ON` will "alert" that backports are needed, but it may break CI in pull requests for unrelated reasons.
* `-DCMAKE_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR=OFF` will not "alert" that backports are needed, but it will not cause unrelated failures.

> Maybe we should re-visit this and exclude the errors there?

For CMake warnings as errors, it's not `CMAKE_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR` but rather [`-Wno-error`](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/manual/cmake.1.html#cmdoption-cmake-Werror).
https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/pull/477 was just merged, so hopefully this won't happen again in the future 🙏
